candidates.tagline: Apple's first foldable cracked at the hinge within hours — Samsung says 'welcome'
candidates.story: Apple's $1,999 iPhone Duo — its first-ever foldable, launched October 23, 2026 — has inner displays cracking along the hinge within hours of unboxing; iFixit's teardown identified a hidden flaw where a display cable crosses a central support bar under the screen, and Samsung immediately launched global billboards saying 'Welcome to Foldables' and 'folding since 2019.'
candidates.why_funny: Apple spent years refusing to make a foldable until it got it right, while Samsung built seven generations of them — and Apple's very first attempt cracked before most users had opened it twice.
candidates.alt: An open iPhone Duo foldable held in a hand, showing a bright white horizontal crack line running across the inner display right at the hinge point, with Chinese iOS widgets visible around it

candidates.tagline: Skims' $148 advent calendar: 12 days of bobby pins, keychains, and scrunchies
candidates.story: Kim Kardashian's Skims brand sold a $148 'Accessories Advent Calendar' in November 2026; unboxing TikToks — including one that got 18.9 million views — revealed 12 compartments containing SKIMS-branded bobby pins, hair clips, scrunchies, keychains, a compact mirror, and a squishy toy, with no clothing; Skims has since offered every buyer a full refund after the 'Temu junk' backlash.
candidates.why_funny: An advent calendar is supposed to build excitement with increasingly valuable daily reveals — Skims managed to make $148 of hair accessories feel like they arrived in a Temu haul, then had to issue refunds to anyone who pointed that out.
candidates.alt: Split image: left shows TikToker holding the cute red-and-pink 2026 Skims Advent Calendar box with a deer motif; right shows all 12 contents dumped on the floor — a pile of scrunchies, hair ties, plastic keychains, and a red SKIMS logo keyring
